newsitem.title: CANADA: Potash Corp. falls on Arcadian takeover news.
newsitem.headline: Potash Corp. falls on Arcadian takeover news.

text.p: Shares of Canadian fertiliser giant Potash Corp. of Saskatchewan Inc. fell on Tuesday, the first day of trading after the company said it was buying U.S. nitrogen concern Arcadian Corp. in a cash and stock deal.

The $1.18 billion Potash bid, which eclipsed a proposed merger between Arcadian and Freeport-McMoRan Inc., was aimed at adding nitrogen to Potash's product slate, a move that would see it becoming a top global producer of all three nutrients.
The definitive agreement was announced on the U.S. Labour Day holiday on Monday. Potash fell C$3.25 to C$100.25 in Toronto and by $2.38 to $73.63 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Saskatoon, Saskatchewan-based Potash Corp., already a world powerhouse in potash and phosphate production, had long been speculated as a suitor for various North American nitrogen-based fertiliser producers.
Analysts on Tuesday said a $25 million breakup fee that would be paid to Potash if the takeover failed to go ahead made the chances of another competing offer slim.
With Arcadian shares in New York trading at $24.63 on Tuesday, below the Potash offer of $25 to $27 per share, investors also appeared to be expecting no sweetened bid.
Chuck Childers, Potash Corp.'s chairman, president and chief executive, said in an interview that Arcadian's size and low share price made for an attractive acquisition.

"They are the largest (nitrogen producer) in the Western Hemisphere," Childers said. "It's been our strategy and our operating procedure to try and be as big a force as we can in any of the commodities we get into."
The move follows a string of recent and planned acquisitions for Potash Corp.
The company made two large phosphate purchases in the United States last year for a total of $1.1 billion.
Potash also said last month it was in talks to buy BASF AG's 51-percent stake in German potash company Kali und Salz AG for about $365 million.
Childers said the acquisition would be boost net earnings per share by 25 percent, based on forecasts by seven prominent fertiliser analysts.
Vahid Fathi, analyst with Everen Securities in Chicago, said he downgraded Potash Corp. on Tuesday to short-term market underperformer from short-term market performer following the acquisition news.
Fathi noted that nitrogen is much more volatile in pricing than phosphate and potash.
Arcadian Chief Executive Doug Campbell, however, told a conference call that the deal would help decrease the price volatility in fertiliser products.
The deal was expected to be closed within four months.
